items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: I did a tour of one-night stands with Benny Carter. And at the end of the tour, he had a record session... he asked me to sing a couple of selections on it.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. Well I did a tour of one-night stands with Benny Carter. And at the end of the tour, he had a record session. And we sort of stayed up all night recording these things. This was the first -- well, not actually, because if you want to say a big band, the first one was with John Kirby -- I mean with Claude Thornhill, the very beginning. But this was my first big band recording session. It was Benny's session, but he asked me to sing a couple of selections on it.
Very refreshing kind of change, too, from some of the other materials.

items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: the first record date that I had used John Kirby's men, he had along with Babe, Pete Brown, alto Man, and Frankie Newton.

ctx.x: Well that's the information I have from the Encyclopedia of Jazz.

Well, I think that how Babe Russin got in on the gig, Claude must have known him because I knew none of the musicians before I came to New York. You know, I didn't even know Kirby that well and his group. In fact, the first record date that I had used John Kirby's men, he had along with Babe, Pete Brown, alto Man, and Frankie Newton. He hadn't got a hold of Charlie Shavers and Russell Procope at that time. In fact, I think that Billy Kyle, Russell Procope, and Charlie with out on the road with Lucky Millinder and…
